title: Savoy Bus Overturns, 11 Students Injured
text:
Savoy Bus Overturns, 11 Students Injured

SAVOY — A Savoy school bus loaded with about 25 students overturned on a winding country road Thursday about 3 p.m. injuring 11 students and the driver. None were seriously hurt however, though one remained hospitalized today for observation.

The accident occurred on a loosely graveled road a mile and a half south of the Savoy school. Three or four students had been let off before the accident occurred.

The driver, Jack Morgan, scrambled out the driver's side window aiding students, while students in turn aided each other in getting out of the bus.

Jennifer Francis' hand was pinned between the top of the bus window and the ground. Morgan and a couple of students dug the dirt from around her hand to free it.

About that time Steve Reynolds, Bells, passed by on his motorcycle and drove on to a neighboring home to sound the alarm. Fannin County Deputies and Savoy Policeman Don Freeman hurried to the scene along with a wrecker.

Principal Richard Owmby said seven children were taken to the Fannin County hospital in Bonham, and four children were taken to the Medical Plaza Hospital in Sherman, along with the bus driver.

Owmby said only one student still was hospitalized. He was identified as Carl Bowhay, 16, a junior. He received a bruise above the kidney and is being held in the Fannin County hospital for observation.

Treated and released from Fannin County hospital were the following students:

Theo Dettmer, 6, head injury.
Lisa Harvey, 15, neck injury.
Heidi Bowhay, 12, bruise over jaw.
Jeff Francis, 11, bruises on body.
Sheri Melguin, 8, bump on head.
Gerry Dettmer, 12, bruises.

Treated and released from the Medical Plaza hospital were:

Keith Thomas, 7, bruise on leg.

Donna Francis, 8, broken tooth, one tooth knocked out, cuts.

Jennifer Francis, 9, bruises.

Denise Ballard, wrist and finger injured.

Jack Morgan, 70, driver of the bus, bruises and cuts.

Owmby said Morgan told him that two girls were standing up in the bus. When Morgan spotted them in his rearview mirror, he told them to sit down. In the few seconds it took Morgan to get the girls seated, the front wheels of the bus dipped over the right side of the humpback road.

Morgan told Owmby that as he attempted to make the curve in the narrow road, the rear wheels hit a bump and the next thing he knew the bus was on its side sliding down the hill. It slid about 200 feet before finally coming to a halt.

The mother of the Francis children was first at the scene. She took the four students to Sherman, including two of her own children, but missed her son, Jeff, who wound up at the Bonham hospital.

Morgan has been driving a Savoy school bus for the past 12 years. He is a retired truck driver.

The students not injured were taken home by either the deputies or other residents who came to the scene to give aid and check on the condition of students.

The bus is the newest owned by the system, purchased just six months ago. It was not heavily damaged though the windshield on the passenger side was cracked, along with a dent near the student steps.

As word of the accident spread, dozens of spectators from the area drove to the scene. The country road was covered with automobiles for about an hour.
